# Herdr: coalesce the per-refresh `wl` spawns into one consolidated read

## Problem statement

A Herdr default-view refresh runs **five separate `wl` subprocesses per pane per tick**: the four mandatory `wl list` subsets plus the `wl next` browse feed (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`). Per-spawn Node bootstrap now dominates the cost (~66 % of the remaining 0.70 CPU-s/spawn is the bare-node floor), so F10 capped the achievable reduction at ~65 % with five spawns and missed the 60 % target (47.6 % achieved). The remaining lever is **fewer spawns**: one consolidated read per refresh tick.

## Users

- **Herdr pane operator** (producer/agent running several Herdr panes on one worklog): wants a responsive worklist without each pane burning CPU on five `wl` boots per tick.
- **Herdr plugin maintainer**: wants one simple, cacheable read seam instead of five coordinated queries with an in-flight memo.
- **wl CLI maintainer**: wants the consolidated command to reuse the existing DB-query and read-cache machinery, not fork it.

### Example user stories

- As a Herdr pane operator, when 4–5 panes refresh every 30 s against one shared worklog, total CPU consumption should drop to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline** so the host stays responsive.
- As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want `fetcher.ts` to issue **one `wl` read per refresh tick** (one DB open, one cache entry), with the displayed items unchanged.
- As an agent relying on the worklist, I want the **mandatory guarantees** (critical items, blocked items and the review queue always shown) preserved by tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single `wl` invocation returns every subset the worklist needs — critical, in_review review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots and the browse feed — as a **dedicated `wl worklist --json` command** (preferred) or an equivalent `--worklist-bundle` mode, sharing **one DB open and one read-cache entry**.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` issues that single read per default-view refresh tick; the mandatory-subset guarantees (critical always shown, blocked always shown, review queue always shown) are preserved by tests.
- Measured with `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10): total CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle with 4 panes drops to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline (≤ 63.8 CPU-s)**, ideally ~5× fewer spawns.
- Cache correctness unchanged: identical JSON for identical DB state, write invalidation still bumps the state counter, and worktree / `--worklog-dir` behaviour is unchanged.
- Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state (existing fetcher tests + the spawn-reduction simulation pass).
- **Testing/validation:** new tests cover the consolidated command's response shape, read-cache hit and write-invalidation, the fetcher's single-spawn path, mandatory-subset guarantees and output parity with the per-subset path.
- **Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (notably `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`).
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Pure read:** the bundle must not write. `wl next`'s auto re-sort is a write byproduct; the bundle must use `--no-re-sort`-style selection (or reuse the selection logic without the write) so the result is deterministically cacheable.
- **Cache reuse:** register the new invocation with the existing read-cache (`src/read-cache-cli.ts`), keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)` and fingerprinted by the monotonic state counter; a mid-action write must not cache an unrepresentative payload.
- **Fail-open fallback:** if the consolidated read is unavailable or fails (older `wl`, malformed payload), the fetcher falls back to today's per-subset spawn path with unchanged behaviour.
- **No output change:** the consolidated response must feed the same `extractItems` → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems` pipeline so ordering, grouping and audit enrichment are identical.
- **Bounded payload:** the browse feed stays limited by the caller's count; subsets are returned with the same filters (`--root-only` where applicable) so payload growth is bounded and no item duplication is unbounded.
- `--worklog-dir` (module override and per-call) and managed-worktree resolution semantics are unchanged.
- TypeScript/Node stack; match existing style; no new runtime dependency unless unavoidable.

## Existing state

- **fetcher.ts** — `fetchMandatorySubsets()` spawns four `wl list` queries in parallel (critical, review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots); `fetchNextItems()` spawns `wl next` and calls `fetchMandatorySubsets()`, giving five spawns per default-view refresh. An in-flight fetch memo deduplicates *identical* concurrent reads (which collapses the review-queue state query into the review subset), and `fetchChildrenForItems` / `fetchActionableCount` already read in-process from SQLite via one refresh-scoped connection.
- **Read cache** — `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` serve `list`, `next`, `show`, `search` and `status` JSON from a shared on-disk cache keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)`, fingerprinted by a monotonic per-worklog-dir write counter; writes bump the counter and drop entries. `src/cli.ts` performs the lookup before loading the heavy command graph.
- **CLI commands** — `src/commands/*.ts` register subcommands through `src/plugin-types.ts` / `src/command-registry.ts`; `next.ts` owns the auto re-sort and the selection semantics; `list.ts` owns the filtered list queries.
- **Measurement** — `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10, 4 panes × 30 s × 5 s tick, sums per-process CPU from spawn records) and `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` (spawn-count/latency per refresh).
- **F10 numbers** — pre-F4 baseline 159.44 CPU-s/cycle, after F4–F7 83.58 CPU-s/cycle (47.6 % reduction), target 63.78; per-spawn 1.329 → 0.697 CPU-s against a ~0.46 CPU-s bare-node floor.

## Desired change

1. Add a consolidated worklist read to the `wl` CLI — preferably a new `wl worklist --json` command — that opens the database **once** and returns the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root, blocked-root and browse-feed subsets in one payload, built from the same query/selection code the individual commands use.
2. Make it a cacheable read invocation (one cache entry, same state-counter fingerprint and write invalidation), so repeat refreshes across panes hit the cache as a single entry.
3. Change `fetcher.ts` so the default-view refresh drives that one read (with the review-queue state and browse feed derived from it) and retains the existing per-subset path as a fail-open fallback.
4. Add coverage: command unit/integration tests, cache hit/invalidation tests, fetcher single-spawn and mandatory-guarantee tests, and an output-parity test against the per-subset path; update the spawn-reduction simulation and the benchmark expectations.
5. Update `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` and any CLI reference docs/comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — **new** consolidated read command (or a `--worklist-bundle` mode added to `src/commands/list.ts`)
- `src/command-registry.ts` — register the new command
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — add the invocation to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` / cacheability checks
- `src/cli.ts` — cache lookup path (expected unchanged; verify the new command is served before the heavy graph)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — single consolidated read, review-state/browse derivation, fail-open fallback
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `doRefresh` wiring so the bundle replaces the per-subset fan-out
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` — spawn-reduction simulation uses the consolidated invocation
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-*.test.ts` — mandatory-subset, review-queue and output-parity coverage
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` — measurement harness (expects the consolidated query)
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — cold-refresh cost section updated

## Related work

- **F10 — WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J** (completed): measured the <= 60 % shortfall and filed this item with the spawn-count lever. This item is the follow-up implementation of that lever.
- **WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B** (completed, outbound dependency): spawn-load epic — transient `wl` process CPU usage.
- **WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG** (completed): cut cold refresh cost — in-process SQLite reads, in-flight fetch memo, batched expanded children. The consolidated read builds on this.
- **WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B** (completed): one shared in-process connection per refresh — related "one open per refresh" precedent.
- **WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN** (completed): make Herdr refresh snappy after agent updates — parent of the earlier performance work.
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/wl-spawn-baseline-2026-10-19.md`, `docs/benchmarks/wal-read-latency-benchmark.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Cache staleness (risk, high):** a single cache entry must never serve stale data across a write. Mitigation: reuse the counter fingerprint, cache only when the counter is unchanged since lookup, and add an explicit write-invalidation test.
- **Re-sort write byproduct (risk, medium):** today's `wl next` runs an auto re-sort (a DB write) on some invocations. The bundle must be a pure read; assumption: `--no-re-sort` selection produces the same displayed order for a stable DB. Verify with an output-parity test; if ordering genuinely differs, resolve the re-sort as a separate, explicitly-documented concern rather than making the bundle a write.
- **Mandatory-subset regression (risk, high):** a bundle that silently drops a subset breaks the always-shown guarantees. Mitigation: tests assert each mandatory subset is present regardless of the browse window.
- **Backwards compatibility (risk, low):** an older `wl` without the new command. Mitigation: fall back to the per-subset spawn path (fail-open).
- **Cross-subset consistency (risk, medium):** the five subsets are read in one process but through separate queries; a write landing mid-bundle could make the subsets disagree. Mitigation: serve all subsets from one DB connection inside a read transaction (or the same store snapshot) so the payload reflects one stable state; at minimum, match today's eventual-consistency behaviour and document it.
- **Payload size (risk, low):** five subsets in one payload. Mitigation: keep the browse feed count-bounded and reuse the existing dedupe/merge pipeline.
- **Scope creep (risk, medium):** further per-spawn startup optimisation (F4–F7) is out of scope. Record additional opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** `wl` and the Herdr plugin ship together from this repository, so the fetcher may rely on the new command in the same release; the fallback remains for robustness.

## Verification plan

```sh
# CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle, 4 panes (F10 harness)
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh -- --json --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5

# Spawn count and latency for a single default-view refresh
npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json
```

- Compare the measured CPU-seconds against the ≤ 63.8 CPU-s target and the pre-F4 baseline quoted above.
- Run the changed-scope and full test suites via `/skill:test`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Was an interview needed for this intake?
  **A (agent, based on repo evidence):** No. The seed context already contains a measured problem, a quantified target, explicit acceptance criteria and a named lever, so the brief was drafted directly from that plus a repo inspection. Source: work item description and F10 comment.
- **Q:** Which command shape should the consolidated read take?
  **A (agent, derived from work item AC):** The AC permits either a `--worklist-bundle` mode or a dedicated command; this brief records a dedicated `wl worklist --json` command as the preferred option (cleaner cache key, no change to `list`/`next` semantics). Source: work item AC 1.
- **Q:** Does the browse feed's auto re-sort write belong in the bundle?
  **A (agent, derived from `src/commands/next.ts`):** The bundle must be a pure read to be deterministically cacheable, so it uses `--no-re-sort`-style selection and the re-sort is treated as a separate concern; output parity is guarded by a test. Recorded as a risk above. Source: `src/commands/next.ts` auto re-sort logic.
- **Q:** Is a fail-open fallback required?
  **A (agent, derived from existing fetcher design):** Yes — the fetcher's existing in-process fast paths all fail open to `wl` spawns; the consolidated read follows the same convention. Source: `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J** – Verify >=60% CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle (completed)
- **WL-0MSHJ2NWZ000P3X9** – [test-failure] read-cache spawn reduction (6-pane simulation) cuts work spawns by ≥60% across a simulated 6-pane refresh — failing test (completed)
- **WL-0MVFRR98A008MM19** – Spawn instrumentation: per-process CPU and RSS (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, always, bare, baseline, behaviour (+101 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: always, bare, baseline, behaviour, bench (+92 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: achieved, always, bare, behaviour, blocked (+86 more)

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-21T11:11Z** — `plan` skill (agent `plan`, session `herdr-1792579182-3452759-11361`) decomposed the item into **six** child features in test-first dependency order:
  `WL-0MVI0HH740065Z2T` (verification harness) → `WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF` (`wl worklist` command) → {`WL-0MVI0IS6Y0028KTO` (read cache), `WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78` (fetcher + fallback)} → `WL-0MVI0IW8V007DFM6` (`doRefresh` wiring) → `WL-0MVI0IX6E000N6IZ` (docs + benchmark evidence). Dependency edges wired to match.
- **2026-10-21T11:18Z** — Acceptance Criteria section converted from a numbered list to a bullet list so the shared `tree_coverage` helper parses all 8 parent ACs (a numbered list parsed as zero ACs, making the coverage review vacuous). Each child gained explicit `Traceability to parent AC<n>` acceptance bullets. Coverage review result: **8/8 parent ACs covered, 0 uncovered, 0 conflicts, action `proceed`**; stage advanced to `plan_complete`.
- **2026-10-21T11:20Z** — Effort/risk refreshed for the decomposed plan: effort **Small** (expected 8.66 h, recommended 12.66 h), risk **Medium** (score 9/25), confidence 92% (comment `WL-C0MVI0U0F6009D0CW`).

## Appendix: Plan session questions & answers (2026-10-21)

- **Q:** Does planning need a new interview round?
  **A (agent, repo evidence):** No. The intake Appendix already settled the command shape (`wl worklist --json`), the pure-read/`--no-re-sort` treatment, and the fail-open fallback. The effort/risk pre-check returned `decision: plan` (effort Small, risk High) and the approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (approval is requested only for Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk), so no producer confirmation pause was required. Source: `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed` and `plan-approval-gate` output, 2026-10-21T11:0xZ.
- **Q:** Does the consolidated read also serve the stage-filtered and priority-filtered worklist views?
  **A (agent, derived from parent AC2 and `fetchItemsForView`):** No. Parent AC2 scopes the change to the *default-view refresh tick*; the stage, priority and recent-dispatches views keep their existing reads. Recorded as an explicit acceptance criterion in `WL-0MVI0IW8V007DFM6`.
- **Q:** How is browse-feed parity with `wl next` guaranteed without its auto re-sort write?
  **A (agent, derived from `src/commands/next.ts`):** The command performs `--no-re-sort`-style selection (never calls `reSort`) and parity is enforced by an output-parity test comparing the bundle path and the per-subset path on the same DB state (`WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78`). The re-sort remains a separate, explicitly-documented concern as recorded in the intake risks.
- **Q:** Where does the browse-feed selection logic live so `next.ts` is not forked?
  **A (agent, derived from `src/commands/next.ts`):** The post-`findNextWorkItems` pipeline (child-count/audit enrichment, group assignment and group sort) is extracted into a shared module consumed by both `next` and the new `worklist` command (`WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF`, reusing `assignItemGroups`/`compareGroupedItems` from `src/commands/grouping.ts`).
- **Q:** How is the "one DB open" requirement verified rather than assumed?
  **A (agent, design decision):** A spy/counter test asserts exactly one database handle is opened per `wl worklist` invocation, and a separate test asserts the command never bumps the read-cache state counter (pure read). Recorded as acceptance criteria in `WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF`.
- **OPEN QUESTION:** none outstanding. The `Traceability to parent AC<n>` bullets added to child items are coverage traceability, not additional scope.

## Failure Signature

- Test file: `tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts`
- Test case: `entry-point split — fast path > records --version as a version spawn and prints the package version`
- Failure: `AssertionError: --version must record exactly one version spawn record: expected +0 to be 1`

## Root Cause (investigated by plan)

`tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts` selects its CLI under test with
`resolveStartupTarget('auto', repoRoot)` (see `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`).
`auto` **prefers `dist/cli.js` when that built file exists**, falling back to
`src/cli.ts` only on an unbuilt checkout.

The checked-out `dist/cli.js` was built at **2026-10-19 21:21**, before
commit `896d8ad2` (WL-0MVFRRGGC001IQK1, 2026-10-20 04:59) added the
`--version` spawn instrumentation to `src/cli.ts`:

```ts
// src/cli.ts:568-570
if (!cacheServed && (cacheArgv.includes('--version') || cacheArgv.includes('-V'))) {
  recordSpawn('version');
}
```

The stale `dist/cli.js` has `recordSpawn('read-work')` but **no
`recordSpawn('version')`** call, so the spawned CLI records no `version`
spawn record and the assertion `expected +0 to be 1` fires.

`dist/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:86`) and `npm test` does not rebuild it,
so any checkout whose `dist/` predates the `src/` change exhibits this
failure even though the source is correct.

**Conclusion:** the source is correct; the observed failure is a stale-build
artefact of the `auto` target selection, not a source defect.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. From a checkout where `dist/cli.js` predates the `src/cli.ts` version
   instrumentation (`git log --oneline -1 -- src/cli.ts` newer than the
   mtime of `dist/cli.js`):
   - `npx vitest run tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts -t 'records --version as a version spawn'`
2. Observe: `expected +0 to be 1`.
3. Rebuild the CLI (`npm run build`) and re-run the same test — it passes.

## Candidate Remediations (for implementation)

- **A — Rebuild before testing (primary):** ensure `dist/cli.js` is rebuilt
  from HEAD before the suite runs, so `auto` never selects a stale build.
  Preferred fix is that the test/CI path rebuilds (or the test verifies build
  freshness) rather than relying on a manually-built `dist`.
- **B — Fail loudly on stale dist:** make `resolveStartupTarget('auto', …)`
  (or the test setup) detect a `dist/cli.js` older than the newest `src/**`
  file and either rebuild or fall back to `src`, so a stale build cannot
  silently produce a false test failure.
- **C — Test-only hardening:** assert build freshness in
  `entry-point-split.test.ts` so the failure message names the stale build
  instead of the downstream spawn-count assertion.

Remediation A is the minimum end-to-end slice; B prevents recurrence for all
tests that use `auto`.

## Impact

Failing test detected during an automated run. Blocks a green suite for the
agent's current work item and can block PR creation. Not a product defect
once `dist/cli.js` is current.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npx vitest run tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts` passes against the
   latest `dev` with `dist/cli.js` rebuilt from HEAD (`auto` target).
2. The chosen remediation prevents recurrence: a stale `dist/cli.js` either
   cannot be selected by the `auto` target or produces an explicit
   stale-build failure rather than a misleading spawn-count assertion.
3. Any documentation describing the test/benchmark `auto`/`dist`/`src`
   target selection is updated to note the build-freshness requirement.
4. Full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Links

- Test: `tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts`
- Target selection: `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` (`resolveStartupTarget`)
- Version instrumentation: `src/cli.ts:568-570`, `src/spawn-counter.ts`
- Predecessor commit introducing the instrumentation: `896d8ad2`
- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md

## Key Files

- `tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts`
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` (`resolveStartupTarget`)
- `docs/dev/wl-startup-import-budget.md` (AC3 docs update)

## Failure Signature

- Test name: `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` > read-cache spawn reduction (6-pane simulation) > cuts work spawns by ≥60% across a simulated 6-pane refresh
- Failure type: **timeout**, not an assertion failure — the test never reached its ≥60% assertion
- Failing commit: (not available) — observed in a post-push full-suite run on `dev`, 2026-10-20
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
Error: Test timed out in 300000ms. If this is a long-running test, pass a timeout value as the last argument or configure it globally with testTimeout.
```

### Verified during planning (2026-10-20, `dev` @ `bec96e2b`)

- **The failure is wall-clock, not behavioural.** The test's own budget is
  already `300_000` ms (`it(..., 300_000)`) and the seeding `beforeEach` hook
  has `180_000` ms. Exceeding 300 s means no assertion executed, so this
  evidence does **not** implicate the read-cache reduction behaviour — only
  the test's cost.
- **Independent timing baseline.** `test-timings.json`
  (generated 2026-10-20T05:04:37Z) records this test at **203 188 ms
  (203 s)** — the slowest single test in the repository, ahead of
  `sync-vs-mutation` (163 s) and `read-cache-e2e` (146 s).
- **Spawn arithmetic.** The test performs 5 seeding
  `tsx src/cli.ts create` subprocesses + the baseline phase (6 panes × 5
  queries = 30) + the cached phase (6 panes × 5 queries = 30) = **65 `tsx`
  subprocesses**, each a cold Node + tsx start (~3 s average at the recorded
  203 s total).
- **Contention amplifier.** `vitest.config.ts` runs `pool: 'forks'` with
  `maxWorkers: 4`, so up to four spawn-heavy test files start `tsx`
  concurrently; per-spawn cost rises well above the isolated ~3 s, which is
  how a 203 s test exceeds its 300 s budget.
- **Recurrence #3.** This test has already produced two closed test-failure
  items — WL-0MSGS55JL0006A4S (worktree `tsx` ENOENT, fixed by
  `resolveTsxBin()`) and WL-0MSHJ2NWZ000P3X9 (10 s hook timeout → hook
  raised to 180 s, test to 300 s in commit `2e64aacf`). Both were
  timeout/wiring band-aids; the underlying spawn cost was never addressed,
  so the failure has now returned at the raised ceiling.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Check out `dev` (or the relevant worktree) with dependencies installed.
2. Run the failing test: `npm --silent test -- tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`
   (this is a TypeScript/vitest test — the `pytest -q -r a ... -k '<name>'`
   form in the auto-generated triage template does not apply to this file).
3. Observe either the 300 s `Test timed out` failure, or a 200 s+ pass on a
   less loaded machine; capture the test's own summary line
   `[spawn-reduction] panes=6 queries=5 baselineWork=… cachedWork=…
   cacheHits=… reduction=…% (target ≥60%)` from stdout.
4. For the contention path, run the full canonical suite
   (`npm --silent test -- tests/cli`) rather than the file in isolation —
   both prior occurrences passed in isolation and failed under suite load.

## Impact

The slowest single test in the repository (203 s, ~8% of aggregate suite
test-time) intermittently times out and turns `dev` red, blocking PR
creation and making every implement/test/audit gate flaky and slow. Because
the failure is a timeout rather than an assertion failure, re-running
"to confirm flakiness" (the standard triage step) burns another 3-10 minutes
without changing the outcome.

## Root cause analysis (hypothesis — to be confirmed during implementation)

- The read-cache logic is **not** implicated: the timeout pre-empts the
  `expect(cachedWork).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0.4 * baselineWork)` assertion, and
  the same assertions passed on the finish-gate run that preceded the
  recorded failure.
- The dominant cost is **process startup, not cache behaviour**: 65 cold
  `tsx` starts inside one test, amplified by up to 4-way worker contention.
- **Timeouts have already been raised twice** (vitest default 30 s →
  180 s hook / 300 s test in `2e64aacf`). The measured wall clock has now
  outgrown the raised budget, so a third raise is not a fix: it moves the
  ceiling, lengthens every gate further, and leaves the flakiness in place.

## Approach options (implementer to evaluate — do not assume)

1. **Batch the query set per pane.** Drive all 5 herdr queries for a pane in
   a single `tsx` invocation via a small test-only driver, keeping each pane
   a separate process → 12 spawns instead of 60, preserving the
   cross-process property the test exists to measure.
2. **Reduce redundant work.** Seed via the existing helper/`cli-helpers.ts`
   paths rather than 5 separate `tsx create` subprocesses, and check whether
   the baseline and cached phases can share seeded state.
3. **In-process harness.** `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` exists and is used by
   several CLI tests. Viable **only** if it still exercises the
   cross-process *on-disk* cache (`WL_CACHE_DIR`, `src/read-cache.ts`): the
   whole point is that panes are separate processes sharing one cache
   directory, so an in-memory layer would make the ≥60% assertion vacuous.
   Note `recordSpawn` is invoked by CLI code (`src/cli.ts:560`,
   `src/read-cache-cli.ts:173/176`), so counters stay honest in-process.
4. **Long-run group.** Move to the `*.long.test.ts` convention only if none
   of the above preserves the measurement cheaply; record it explicitly as a
   deliberate coverage decision, not a silent skip.

## Constraints

- **No third timeout raise as the fix.** Justify with measurements if a
  budget change is made anyway.
- **Preserve the measurement's intent:** the test must keep asserting ≥60%
  fewer `read-work` spawns and >0 `cache-hit`s across panes sharing one cache
  directory. Any reduction in simulated panes or queries must be justified
  against the parent target (WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA AC7: 6 panes, herdr's real
  query set) and recorded on this item.
- **No production-code change** unless a genuine cache defect is proven.
- **Coordinate, don't duplicate:** suite-wide test-speed optimisation is
  owned by WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 (in progress); this item's scope is making
  *this* test pass deterministically.
- Tests are run only through the standard test skill (`/skill:test`); no
  ad-hoc test invocation.
- Work lands on `dev` only, via the standard worktree/implement flow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts > read-cache spawn reduction (6-pane simulation) > cuts work spawns by ≥60% across a simulated 6-pane refresh` passes against the latest `dev`, both in isolation and under the full-suite/parallel-load conditions that produced this failure.
- The test's runtime is reduced so it completes well inside its configured budget on a loaded host, and the achieved runtime (with the command and host conditions used) is recorded on this item.
- The ≥60% spawn-reduction assertion and the >0 cache-hit assertion are unchanged in intent, and any reduction in simulated panes or queries is justified against the parent target (WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA AC7) and recorded on this item.
- No third timeout raise is used as the fix; if a timeout or hook budget is changed anyway, it is justified with before/after measurements and recorded on this item.
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes, green on repeated CI-like runs without an intermittent timeout for this test.
- Related documentation is updated where it describes this test: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` § "Spawn instrumentation (spawn-reduction measurement)", the test file's header comment, and code comments for any new helper.

## Key Files

**Key Files:** the files an implementer will touch — every path verified to exist on `dev` @ `bec96e2b`.

- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` — the failing test: 6-pane simulation, `300_000` ms budget, 65 `tsx` spawns.
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — `writeConfig`, `writeInitSemaphore` seeding helpers used by the test.
- `tests/test-utils.ts` — `createTempDir`, `cleanupTempDir`, `resolveTsxBin` (added by WL-0MSGS55JL0006A4S).
- `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` — in-process CLI harness (option 3 above).
- `src/cli.ts` — read-cache env plumbing (`WL_CACHE_DISABLED`/`WL_CACHE_TTL_MS`/`WL_CACHE_DIR`, lines ~262-267) and the `recordSpawn('read-work')` baseline path (line ~560).
- `src/read-cache.ts` — on-disk shared cache (`WL_CACHE_DIR` precedence, line ~445).
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — `cache-hit` / `read-work` spawn recording (lines ~173-176).
- `src/spawn-counter.ts` — `countSpawnRecords`, the assertion's data source.
- `./vitest.config.ts` — `pool: 'forks'`, `maxWorkers: 4`, `testTimeout`, long-run exclusions.
- `./package.json` — `test` and `test:timings` scripts.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — § "Spawn instrumentation (spawn-reduction measurement)" explicitly references this test.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8** (in progress, `plan_complete`) — "Reduce time to run
  tests". Names this test as the #1 offender (203 s) and owns the broader
  suite-speed work (baseline capture, mocking spawned `wl` processes,
  long-run grouping). **Overlap:** its AC3 (triage every test ≥5 s) and AC2
  (≥30% suite reduction) touch this test. This item stays the narrow,
  critical fix; anything broader (config changes, other slow files) belongs
  to that epic.
- **WL-0MSHJ2NWZ000P3X9** (completed) — prior occurrence; raised the hook to
  180 s and the test to 300 s (`2e64aacf`). Its band-aid is why the failure
  returned at the new ceiling.
- **WL-0MSGS55JL0006A4S** (completed) — prior occurrence; worktree `tsx`
  ENOENT, fixed by `resolveTsxBin()` in `tests/test-utils.ts`.
- **WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA** (completed) — created this test and its parent
  target (AC7: ≥60% spawn reduction across a 6-pane refresh).
- **WL-0MVGC6JVP00812DS** (in review) — the item whose post-push full-suite
  run surfaced this timeout; also surfaced WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U
  (`entry-point-split` version-record failure), a separate flake.
- Duplicate check performed: no completed item already makes this test pass
  deterministically (both prior occurrences closed on timeout/wiring
  band-aids, not cost), and the owning epic WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 is still in
  progress, so this item is **not** a duplicate — partial overlap recorded
  above.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the work item is an auto-generated
test-failure report (`[test-failure]`, priority critical) whose seed intent
(fix the named failing test) combined with the evidence above makes the
deliverable unambiguous. Derivations recorded instead:

- **Derived (no question needed).** The failure is a timeout, so the fix must
  address test cost/determinism, not cache behaviour. Evidence:
  `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` budgets (`300_000` /
  `180_000` ms) and the timeout excerpt; `test-timings.json` 203 s record.
- **Derived (no question needed).** The repository already has an
  in-process CLI harness (`tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts`), so an in-process
  rewrite is a *candidate*, not an assumption — it is listed as option 3
  with an explicit validity condition (must still exercise the on-disk
  cross-process cache).
- **Derived (no question needed).** The triage template's `pytest -k`
  reproduction command does not apply to a vitest/TypeScript test; corrected
  in **Steps To Reproduce**.
- **OPEN QUESTION (for producer, non-blocking).** Should the fix land on this
  critical item, or be handed to the in-progress epic WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8
  (which owns suite-speed work and names this test as offender #1)? Planning
  interpretation (recorded, not enforced): keep this item as the narrow fix
  so the critical red signal is not absorbed into a broad epic, and record
  the outcome there so the epic does not duplicate it. Producer to confirm or
  redirect at review; no work is blocked.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-20 — `/skill:plan` run (effort/risk pre-check: `skip` — effort Extra
  Small, risk Low per `plan-if-needed`; full estimate post-review: Small,
  Low, 90% confidence). Auto-complete path with six automated review stages:
  - AC alignment: rewrote the template ACs into 6 measurable bullets; 4th
    bullet forbids a third timeout raise as the fix (the two prior
    occurrences closed on timeout/wiring band-aids — WL-0MSHJ2NWZ000P3X9,
    WL-0MSGS55JL0006A4S); 2nd bullet adds a recorded-runtime requirement.
  - Completeness: added **Root cause analysis**, **Approach options** (4
    candidates with validity conditions), **Constraints**, verified **Key
    Files** (12 paths, all exist on `dev` @ `bec96e2b`), **Related work** and
    an Appendix. Corrected the triage template's `pytest -k` reproduction
    command (this is a vitest/TypeScript test).
  - Sequencing/dependencies: no children; test-first intent preserved (the
    test itself is the RED/verification artefact); coordinate-without-duplicate
    guidance against WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 recorded.
  - Scope sizing: single-deliverable fix; noted overlap with the in-progress
    "Reduce time to run tests" epic (offender #1 there).
  - Acceptance & testability: all 6 ACs pass/fail and measurable.
  - Polish & handoff: description restructured for immediate implementation.
  - AC-coverage review: `apply_coverage_review` → `proceed` (0 conflicts),
    stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

# Verify herdr test type and group gate

**Parent:** WL-0MVGJ4WSS005BMSI — Configured test gate excludes the herdr package suite (no herdr test type/group)

## Summary

Test-first verification slice: prove the sanctioned `herdr` test type and named group behave exactly as the parent specifies (parent AC1–AC8), using the test skill's runner (`run_tests.py`) so every run is cache-recorded. Runs after the config child lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `python3 run_tests.py --type herdr --json` (default scope `full`) resolves to `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`, executes it, and records a cache entry under the `herdr` type key — a repeat invocation within the 2h TTL is served from cache (`cached: true`).
- AC2: `python3 run_tests.py --group herdr --json` also works via a `groups.herdr` entry in `.pi/test-config.json`, and the group's `paths` make implement.py's changed-scope gate auto-select the herdr group when a change touches `packages/herdr/`.
- AC3: `python3 run_tests.py --type full --json` still runs exactly `tests/cli` + `tests/unit`; herdr is **not** included in the canonical full suite.
- AC4: `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` defines `types.herdr`; minimum types it omits (`unit`/`smoke`) fail with the runner's loud diagnostic (never a silent full-suite substitution), and `--type full` still works via the suiteCommands fallback.
- AC5: A verification step proves AC1–AC4: run `--type herdr` twice (first cold, second cached), `--group herdr`, `--type full` unchanged, and `--type unit`/`--type smoke` produce the expected loud diagnostics.
- AC6: The full project test suite passes with the new changes (canonical gate green and untouched).

## Minimal Implementation

- Run the AC1–AC4 command matrix and capture the JSON results (cold run, cached re-run, group run, full run, unit/smoke diagnostics); confirm AC6 (full suite green) at the end.
- Triage genuine failures into critical `test-failure` items via the triage helper; do not fix herdr flakiness inside this item.
- Re-measure the herdr suite runtime (`time npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`) and post the figure for the docs child.
- No source or config changes in this child — verification evidence only.

## Dependencies

- Depends on: "Add herdr test type and named group" (config child) — the type/group cannot be verified before they exist.
- Test-first ordering: created before the implementation child; the dependency edge makes it execute after.

## Deliverables

- Comment on the parent with the AC matrix results and measured herdr runtime.
- Triage work items for any genuine failures found.

# Add herdr test type and named group

**Parent:** WL-0MVGJ4WSS005BMSI — Configured test gate excludes the herdr package suite (no herdr test type/group)

## Summary

Add the sanctioned `herdr` test type via the local test-skill extension and the `herdr` named group for changed-scope selection, without touching the canonical `suiteCommands` (producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 preserved).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` defines `types.herdr` with `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`, so `python3 run_tests.py --type herdr --json` (default scope `full`) resolves to that command and records a cache entry under the `herdr` type key; a repeat invocation within the 2h TTL is served from cache (`cached: true`) and never satisfies the audit's full-suite query (only `--type full` scope `full` entries do).
- AC2: `.pi/test-config.json` gains `groups.herdr` with `commands: ["npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src"]` and `paths: ["packages/herdr/**"]`, so `python3 run_tests.py --group herdr --json` works and implement.py's changed-scope gate auto-selects the herdr group when a change touches `packages/herdr/`.
- AC3: The canonical full suite is **unchanged** — `suiteCommands` stays `tests/cli` + `tests/unit`; `run_tests.py --type full` still runs exactly those; herdr is **not** added to `suiteCommands` (producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 preserved).
- AC4: The extension contract is held: `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` defines `types.herdr`; minimum types it omits (`unit`/`smoke`) fail with the runner's loud diagnostic (never a silent full-suite substitution), and `--type full` still works via the suiteCommands fallback.
- AC5: D2 held: both the type and the group land here (not type-only).

## Minimal Implementation

- Create `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` with the `types.herdr` map.
- Add `groups.herdr` (`commands` + `paths`) to `.pi/test-config.json`, leaving `suiteCommands` untouched.
- JSON config only — no source-code changes.
- Do not add herdr to `suiteCommands` or any canonical gate list.

## Dependencies

- None — this is the root change; the verification and docs children depend on it.

## Deliverables

- Updated `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` and `.pi/test-config.json`.
- Comment recording the change; commit message referencing the parent item.

# Herdr downtime dispatch: consume truthful per-slot capacity (lease_state / capacity_hint / prefill ETA)

## Problem statement

The llama-proxy now reports *why* a local slot is unavailable — genuinely
generating, reserved-but-idle, or free — but herdr's downtime dispatcher still
treats any slot with a non-empty `owner_session_id` as busy. In the measurement
window that motivated the proxy change, 2,633 of 2,641 `local_dispatch_denied`
events came from idle lease holders while the GPU decoded only 29.3 % of wall
clock; herdr's `isSlotOwned()` reproduces exactly that false-busy behaviour, so
downtime work is not dispatched while the local model sits idle.

## Users

- **Operator / producer:** wants downtime audits and implements to use the
  local GPU whenever it is genuinely free, rather than waiting for an idle
  lease to expire (or a proxy restart).
- **Downtime dispatcher (herdr plugin):** needs an authoritative,
  machine-readable availability signal instead of inferring busyness from a
  lease owner field.

Example stories:

- As the operator, when the last session's stream has finished but its slot
  lease is still in its post-stream cooldown, herdr should dispatch the next
  downtime pane instead of reporting `slot-owner` for another 20 minutes.
- As the dispatcher, when the proxy says a pool is `idle`, I should not
  require every slot to report `free` before I launch one pane.

## Evidence / existing state (llm-manager)

Upstream capability is **already implemented and deployed** on llm-manager
`dev` (commit `ab00759e`, `LP-0MVGDUVGE0024YAI`). `GET /llama/local/status`
now serves `status_schema_version: 2` and these **additive** fields:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `slots[].lease_state` | `"generating" \| "idle_leased" \| "free"` | `generating` whenever `is_processing`; `idle_leased` when not processing but a live lease still reserves the slot (including post-stream cooldown); `free` otherwise. |
| `slots[].phase` | `"prefill" \| "decode" \| null` | Proxy-side inference; `null` when not processing. |
| `slots[].context_tokens` | `int \| null` | Prompt progress when the llama.cpp build reports it. |
| `slots[].prefill_eta_seconds` | `float \| null` | Calibrated prefill cost of the slot's loaded context, only while `phase === "prefill"`; `null` otherwise or when not computable. |
| `capacity_hint` | `"idle" \| "prefill_bound" \| "saturated"` | One-field pool summary. `idle` = at least one `free` slot **or** every occupied slot is `idle_leased`; `prefill_bound` = no free slot and ≥1 prefill; `saturated` = no free slot and all occupied slots decoding. |
| `prefill_budget_seconds` | `float \| null` | The admission guard's wait budget (configuration constant; stays truthful when slots are stale). |
| `status_schema_version` | `int` | `2` for this payload. |

Contract source: llm-manager `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`
§ "Truthful local capacity: slot phase + prefill ETA". That document names
the herdr `downtime-worker.ts` consumer change as a separate ContextHub
work item (this one).

Relevant existing herdr behaviour (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`):

- `LlamaStatus` / `LlamaSlot` (~lines 620–700) parse `local_active_query`,
  `slots[].is_processing`, `slots[].owner_session_id`, `slots_stale`,
  `contention_queue_depth`.
- `isSlotOwned()` treats **any** non-empty `owner_session_id` as busy;
  `countFreeUnownedSlots()` therefore excludes `idle_leased` slots.
- `evaluateIdle()` requires usable per-slot detail (`slots` non-empty and not
  stale) and fails closed otherwise (`slots-unavailable` / `no-slots`).
- `globalIdleChecks()` requires `local_active_query === false` in all-slots-free
  mode; the spare-capacity path relaxes this to server-up + no model switch.

## Desired change

1. Extend `LlamaStatus` / `LlamaSlot` / `parseLlamaStatus` with the additive
   schema-v2 fields. Keep the parser's existing contract: unknown optional
   fields are ignored; **availability-affecting** values that are malformed
   are ambiguous → fail closed (poll rejected, treated as busy), consistent
   with `slots_stale`; advisory-only values (`phase`, ETAs,
   `context_tokens`) degrade to `undefined`/`null` and never block dispatch.
2. Make `lease_state` the authoritative per-slot busy signal when present:
   - `generating` → **busy** (never eligible).
   - `idle_leased` → **reserved-but-idle**: does **not** consume the free-slot
     budget (it is the false-busy case the upstream change removes).
   - `free` → available.
   - Absent (pre-v2 proxy) → today's behaviour exactly (`owner_session_id`
     presence ⇒ busy).
3. Use `capacity_hint` as a defensive cross-check:
   - `saturated` → never dispatch (no capacity), record a distinct reason.
   - `idle` → pool is genuinely usable; normal free-slot budget still applies.
   - `prefill_bound` → still gated by the free-slot budget here; concurrency
     pacing against the prefill gate is the sibling item
     `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`.
   - Absent → today's behaviour.
4. Record the new evidence in the decision log: `lease_state`-derived
   free/idle-leased counts, `capacity_hint`, per-slot `phase` and
   `prefill_eta_seconds`, and `status_schema_version`. Add a distinct
   no-dispatch reason/token for a genuine prefill/decode saturation (e.g.
   `capacity-saturated` / header `saturated`) so a stop is distinguishable
   from `slot-owner`, `contention`, and `no-slots`.
5. Keep the existing fail-closed contract: if `lease_state` is absent **and**
   `owner_session_id` is present, still treat the slot as busy. Never infer
   availability from `available_slots` alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `parseLlamaStatus` parses `status_schema_version`, `capacity_hint`,
  `prefill_budget_seconds` and per-slot `lease_state`, `phase`,
  `context_tokens`, `prefill_eta_seconds`; a v2 payload round-trips, a v1
  payload (fields absent) parses exactly as today, and malformed optional
  values follow the documented fail-closed/advisory rule without throwing.
- [ ] With `lease_state` present, availability excludes only `generating`
  slots: an `idle_leased` slot counts as available capacity (test), a `free`
  slot counts as available (test), and a `generating` slot never counts
  (test) — including a case where `owner_session_id` is set but
  `lease_state === "idle_leased"` (the regression this item exists to fix).
- [ ] A pre-v2 payload (`lease_state` absent, `owner_session_id` present)

# Herdr downtime dispatch: use the proxy's local_idle_seconds as the idle-age signal

## Problem statement

The llama-proxy now publishes an authoritative local idle age
(`local_idle_seconds`, plus `local_last_activity_at` and
`local_last_activity_source`), but herdr measures idle duration itself from
its own polls. If the GPU has already been idle for hours when herdr starts
polling (plugin restart, pane restart, resumed session), herdr still waits a
full `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` before dispatching; conversely its sampled
tracker can be fooled by gaps in polling. Both outcomes leave the local model
idle when it could be working.

## Users

- **Operator / producer:** wants downtime dispatch to start as soon as the
  local GPU has genuinely been idle long enough, including immediately after
  a herdr restart.
- **Downtime dispatcher (herdr plugin):** wants the proxy's authoritative
  idle age instead of inferring it from poll cadence.

Example stories:

- As the operator, after restarting herdr while the GPU has been idle for two
  hours, I want the next downtime pane dispatched on the first poll rather
  than after another threshold wait.
- As the dispatcher, when the proxy reports `local_idle_seconds` below the
  threshold, I should not dispatch even if my local tracker has an older idle
  run (the proxy is authoritative).

## Evidence / existing state (llm-manager)

Upstream capability is **already implemented and deployed** on llm-manager
`dev` (commit `05986c1b`, `LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J`). `GET /llama/local/status`
now serves:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `local_idle_seconds` | `float \| null` | Monotonic idle age of the local backend; updated on dispatch start, on every forwarded SSE chunk, and on request finish. Baseline is proxy process start, so a freshly restarted proxy reports its true idle age rather than "unknown". |
| `local_last_activity_at` | ISO string \| null | Wall-clock timestamp of the last local activity (operator-facing). |
| `local_last_activity_source` | string \| null | What last touched the backend (`dispatch` / `chunk` / `finish` / startup …). |

The same upstream change also added idle-aware local admission on the proxy
(`local_idle_admit_enabled`, default off), which reads exactly this signal.

Relevant existing herdr behaviour (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`):

- `createIdleTracker()` records idle runs from the worker's own poll results;
  `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` is the continuous-idle threshold.
- Per-slot mode tracks the same N slots continuously free
  (`perSlotTracker.thresholdMetCount`).
- `globalIdleChecks()` requires `local_active_query === false` (all-slots-free
  mode); the spare-capacity path relaxes it.
- `LlamaStatus` does **not** parse `local_idle_seconds`.

Contract source: llm-manager `proxy/docs/routing.md` § "Idle-aware local
admission" (idle signal description) and
`proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`.

## Desired change

1. Extend `LlamaStatus` / `parseLlamaStatus` with `local_idle_seconds`,
   `local_last_activity_at` and `local_last_activity_source` (all optional;
   malformed values degrade to `undefined`, never throw).
2. When `local_idle_seconds` is present and finite, use it as the
   **authoritative** idle-age signal for threshold qualification:
   - `idle_seconds >= thresholdSeconds` → the idle threshold is already met
     on this poll (no need to wait for the local tracker to accumulate).
   - `idle_seconds < thresholdSeconds` → not yet qualified; do **not** admit
     on the strength of an older local tracker run (the proxy is
     authoritative).
   - absent / non-finite → fall back to today's local tracker behaviour
     exactly (pre-feature proxy).
3. Keep the immediate busy reset: a poll that shows activity
   (`is_processing`, a live lease, any contention/gate waiter) still resets
   the idle run regardless of the reported idle age.
4. Use `local_last_activity_source` in the decision log (and optionally the
   header) to explain *why* the backend is considered busy/idle (e.g.
   `chunk`, `dispatch`, `finish`) — this is operator-facing evidence, not a
   gate.
5. Do not weaken the per-slot contract: `local_idle_seconds` is a global
   signal; it may only *satisfy* the per-slot continuous-free requirement
   when the same poll also provides usable per-slot detail and no slot is
   processing/owned. If per-slot detail is absent/empty/stale, the existing
   `slots-unavailable` fail-closed path still applies.
6. Preserve `requiredFreeSlots` semantics: the idle-age signal qualifies the
   *duration*, not the *capacity*; the free-slot budget is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `parseLlamaStatus` reads `local_idle_seconds`,
  `local_last_activity_at` and `local_last_activity_source`; absent fields
  preserve today's behaviour, and malformed values degrade to `undefined`
  without throwing (tests).
- [ ] With `local_idle_seconds >= thresholdSeconds` reported on the first
  poll (fresh worker, usable per-slot detail, no activity), the worker
  dispatches without waiting for the local tracker to accumulate the
  threshold (test).
- [ ] With `local_idle_seconds < thresholdSeconds`, the worker does **not**
  dispatch even when its local tracker already has an older idle run (test).
- [ ] A poll reporting activity (per-slot `is_processing`, live lease, or a
  contention/gate waiter) resets the idle run regardless of a large
  `local_idle_seconds` (test).
- [ ] `local_idle_seconds` absent (pre-feature proxy) restores exactly
  today's local-tracker behaviour (regression test).
- [ ] `slots_stale: true`, `slots: []` or unusable per-slot detail still
  yields `slots-unavailable` even when `local_idle_seconds` is large (test —
  the global signal must not bypass the per-slot fail-closed contract).
- [ ] The decision log records `local_idle_seconds` (and
  `local_last_activity_source` when present) so an operator can see why a
  dispatch was admitted or deferred (test asserts the logged fields).
- [ ] Tests are written red-first and cover every transition above using the
  existing fixtures (`downtime-worker.parse.test.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.idle.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (idle detection description and
  `downtimeIdleThresholdMs`) and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (idle-age
  authority and fallback behaviour).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatible:** absent idle fields must behave exactly as today.
- **Fail closed on ambiguity:** a non-finite/malformed idle age is ignored
  (fallback to the local tracker), never treated as "idle forever".
- **Global signal, local contract:** `local_idle_seconds` never bypasses the
  per-slot availability/fail-closed rules.
- **No new polling:** reuse the existing single-flight status poll.
- Keep the change surgical: prefill/concurrency pacing is the sibling item
  `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`; per-slot `lease_state`/`capacity_hint` availability
  is `WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `LlamaStatus`,
  `parseLlamaStatus`, `createIdleTracker` / tick idle qualification,
  per-slot tick path, decision-log builder, `decisionHeaderToken` if a new
  reason is introduced.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` — new fields,
  malformed/absent cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.test.ts` — threshold
  qualification, busy reset, stale/unusable interplay.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — end-to-end tick and
  decision-log assertions.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` — idle-signal fixtures.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — idle detection contract and threshold.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — idle-age authority.

## Related work

**Upstream (llm-manager)**

- `LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J` — Idle-aware local admission for large/cold prompts —
  completed (`05986c1b`); publishes `local_idle_seconds` and the activity
  source.
- `LP-0MVGDUVGE0024YAI` — truthful capacity payload (`capacity_hint`,
  `lease_state`); the availability sibling.
- `LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ` — prefill serialisation; the pacing sibling.
- `LP-0MVECWYWK000U3E1` — stale log-derived slot-progress expiry; keeps the
  per-slot `n_decoded` signal honest (a related proxy-side fix).

**ContextHub**

- `WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P` — **blocks this item**: truthful per-slot capacity
  parsing/gating.
- `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` — sibling: prefill-serialisation pacing.
- `WL-0MSP28LSY007NDYX` / `WL-0MT3D585I0070FF0` — per-slot idle tracking and
  the relaxed idle gate (the behaviour this item qualifies).
- `WL-0MSL2ZQIF006QB4Q` — `local_active_query` as the local busy signal
  (precedent for preferring a proxy-authoritative signal).
- `WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW` — fail-closed per-slot contract.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Risk — clock/baseline semantics:** `local_idle_seconds` is monotonic and
  proxy-process-relative; a proxy restart resets it to a small value even if
  the GPU was idle before. The local tracker remains a valid fallback, so the
  worker may still wait a threshold after a proxy restart — acceptable and
  documented.
- **Risk — bypassing per-slot continuous-free semantics:** mitigated by
  keeping the per-slot fail-closed preconditions and only using the global
  age as a *duration* qualification.
- **Assumption** — `local_idle_seconds` reflects all local activity
  (dispatch start, chunks, finish), so "idle ≥ threshold" implies every slot
  has been idle that long.
- **Assumption** — `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` remains the user-facing
  threshold; no new setting is needed.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not expand into proxy admission changes
  (`local_idle_admit_enabled`) — that is upstream and off by default.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the upstream implementation and its
published contract fully determine this brief. Evidence reviewed:

- llm-manager `dev` commit `05986c1b`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`
  § "Idle-aware local admission", `proxy/proxy/local_activity.py`.
- llm-manager `LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J` description and acceptance criteria.
- llm-manager `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` `get_llama_local_status()` idle
  fields.
- ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`createIdleTracker`,
  `evaluateIdle`, per-slot tick), `packages/herdr/README.md`,
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- Worklog searches: `local_idle_seconds`, `idle`, `slot` — no existing
  ContextHub idle-age consumer item found (duplicate check performed).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P** – Herdr downtime dispatch: consume truthful per-slot capacity (lease_state / capacity_hint / prefill ETA) (in-progress)
- **WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX** – Herdr downtime dispatch: pace dispatch to local prefill serialisation (blocked)
- **WL-0MUV0VEFW007ZBB7** – Raise default downtime idle threshold to 75s so active sessions reclaim freed slots before dispatch (completed)

# Herdr downtime dispatch: pace dispatch to local prefill serialisation

## Problem statement

The llama-proxy now serialises local prefills (`local_max_concurrent_prefills`
default `1`) and publishes the gate state, but herdr's dispatcher still uses
the free-slot count as its only concurrency budget. With two free slots it can
launch two downtime panes; the second prefill waits behind the first in the
contention queue and may fall back to a remote provider — the GPU is only ever
prefilling one request at a time, and the pane's first turn is spent waiting
instead of using local capacity. Prefill dominates hold time (p50 61.8 s,
p90 269.8 s), so launching during an in-flight prefill is the worst moment to
start.

## Users

- **Operator / producer:** wants each downtime pane to get the local GPU's
  full prefill throughput, not to queue behind a sibling pane.
- **Downtime dispatcher (herdr plugin):** needs to pace concurrency to the
  same gate the proxy enforces, and to know when waiting is futile.

Example stories:

- As the dispatcher, while `local_prefills_in_flight >=
  local_max_concurrent_prefills`, I should not start a new local session —
  it would only queue.
- As the dispatcher, when `prefill_gate_waiters > 0`, I should treat the gate
  as contended and pace the next dispatch, exactly as I already do for
  `contention_queue_depth`.

## Evidence / existing state (llm-manager)

Upstream capability is **already implemented and deployed** on llm-manager
`dev` (commit `42f93580`, `LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ`). `GET /llama/local/status`
now serves, in addition to the existing fields:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `local_prefills_in_flight` | `int` | Prefills currently in flight. |
| `local_max_concurrent_prefills` | `int` | Effective cap; `1` = serialised (default), `0` = gate disabled (cap becomes the slot pool). |
| `prefill_gate_waiters` | `int` | Requests waiting for the prefill gate (the live contention-queue depth). |

The prefill-ETA guard (`LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ`) additionally serves top-level
`prefill_eta_seconds`, `queue_eta_seconds`, `prefill_eta_calibrated`,
`prefill_eta_samples`, and (from `LP-0MVGDUVGE0024YAI`) per-slot
`slots[].prefill_eta_seconds` and `prefill_budget_seconds`.

Measured rationale (2026-10-19 → 2026-10-20, 460 paired local dispatches):
47.8 % of prefills shared the GPU; per-request first-byte p50 was 85.0 s with
one overlap vs 23.4 s alone, while aggregate prefill throughput stayed flat
(~254 tok/s) — concurrency added latency, not capacity.

Relevant existing herdr behaviour (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`):

- `LlamaStatus` parses `contention_queue_depth` (the live queue depth, the
  sole contention gate) and `contention_queued_count` (telemetry only).
- The dispatcher polls `/llama/local/status`, counts free/unowned slots,
  applies `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots`, then dispatches up to the free-slot
  budget within an idle window (`browseItemCount` / audit batching).
- No parser or gate currently reads any prefill-gate field.

Contract source: llm-manager `proxy/docs/routing.md` § "Prefill
serialisation" and `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`.

## Desired change

1. Extend `LlamaStatus` / `parseLlamaStatus` with `local_prefills_in_flight`,
   `local_max_concurrent_prefills`, `prefill_gate_waiters`,
   `prefill_budget_seconds`, `queue_eta_seconds` and per-slot
   `phase` / `prefill_eta_seconds`. Fields absent on a pre-v2/pre-feature
   proxy → `undefined` (no pacing), never a hard failure.
2. Compute an **effective local dispatch budget** each tick:
   `effectiveBudget = min(freeSlotBudget, prefillCapacityBudget)` where
   `prefillCapacityBudget = 0` when
   `local_prefills_in_flight >= local_max_concurrent_prefills` (and
   `local_max_concurrent_prefills > 0`); otherwise the remaining prefill
   headroom (at least 1). When the cap is `0`/absent, the prefill budget is
   unbounded (today's behaviour).
3. Treat `prefill_gate_waiters > 0` as contention evidence equivalent to a
   non-empty `contention_queue_depth`: pace/back off and record a distinct
   reason (e.g. `prefill-gate`) so the stop is observable and distinguishable
   from `contention` / `slot-owner` / `no-slots`.
4. Do not launch a session whose projected wait obviously cannot succeed:
   when the proxy reports `queue_eta_seconds` above `prefill_budget_seconds`
   (both present and finite), or a per-slot prefill ETA above the budget,
   defer the dispatch and record the ETA evidence. This mirrors the proxy's
   own admission guard rather than parking a pane behind a doomed wait.
5. Record the pacing evidence in the decision log: prefill in-flight/cap,
   gate waiters, `capacity_hint`, `queue_eta_seconds`,
   `prefill_budget_seconds`, per-slot `prefill_eta_seconds`, and the reason
   when a dispatch was deferred.
6. Preserve all existing gates and fail-closed behaviour: an unusable
   per-slot signal still yields `slots-unavailable`; pacing can only make the
   dispatcher *more* conservative, never bypass `slots_stale`/malformed
   handling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `parseLlamaStatus` reads `local_prefills_in_flight`,
  `local_max_concurrent_prefills`, `prefill_gate_waiters`,
  `prefill_budget_seconds`, `queue_eta_seconds` and
  `slots[].phase`/`slots[].prefill_eta_seconds`; absent fields leave the
  current behaviour unchanged, and malformed gate fields fail closed
  (poll rejected / no dispatch) consistently with the existing optional
  parser contract (tests).
- [ ] When `local_max_concurrent_prefills > 0` and
  `local_prefills_in_flight >= local_max_concurrent_prefills`, the effective
  dispatch budget is `0` for that tick and no pane is launched; when the
  in-flight count drops below the cap the budget recovers (tests).
- [ ] `prefill_gate_waiters > 0` prevents a new dispatch and is recorded
  with a distinct reason/header token (tests assert the reason and token).
- [ ] A projected wait above the proxy's `prefill_budget_seconds`
  (`queue_eta_seconds` or per-slot prefill ETA) defers the dispatch and the
  decision log carries the ETA evidence; a missing ETA or budget does not
  block dispatch (tests).
- [ ] `local_max_concurrent_prefills` absent or `0` restores exactly today's
  free-slot-only budget (regression test).
- [ ] The decision log includes the prefill-gate fields and
  `capacity_hint` when the proxy serves them (test asserts the logged
  fields).
- [ ] Tests are written red-first against the existing fixtures
  (`downtime-worker.parse.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.idle.test.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`, `downtime-worker.test.ts`) and cover each
  gate transition.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (downtime worker settings /
  prefill pacing) and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (concurrency budget
  contract and the interaction with `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots`).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No new polling:** reuse the existing single-flight status poll.
- **Backward compatible:** absent prefill fields must behave exactly as
  today; the plugin may run against a proxy from before
  `LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ`.
- **Pacing only reduces concurrency:** never raise the existing free-slot
  budget, never bypass the fail-closed per-slot contract, and never dispatch
  when `slots_stale`/`slots: []`.
- **No new configuration knob unless required:** default pacing should follow
  the proxy's own cap and budget. If a local override is needed, name it,
  clamp it, and document it in the README (avoid a second source of truth
  for the budget).
- Keep the change surgical: per-slot availability (`lease_state` /

## Failure Signature

- Test file: `tests/cli/completion.test.ts`
- Failing cases (2 — one per shell):
  - `wl completion bash > contains all known subcommands`
  - `wl completion zsh > contains all known subcommands`
- Failure: `AssertionError: expected completion script to contain "worklist"` — the generated script's command list omits `worklist` (`audit … unlock update completion`, no `worklist`).
- Failing commit: surfaced on `dev` after `c8d8197f` (WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF, 2026-10-21 19:28).
- CI job: (not available)

## Root Cause (verified during planning)

**The source is correct; the failure is a stale-build artefact.** Two facts
combine:

1. **`tests/cli/completion.test.ts` spawns the *built* CLI and bypasses the
   build-freshness guard.** It hard-codes its entry point:

   ```ts
   const CLI_PATH = resolve(__dirname, '../../dist/cli.js');
   ```

   `dist/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:86`) and `npm test` does not rebuild it,
   so this file asserts against whatever build happens to be on disk — not
   against `src/`.

2. **The checked-out `dist/` predated the `worklist` command.** Observed
   state: `dist/cli.js` mtime `2026-10-21 15:52:42`; commits
   `c8d8197f` (19:28:20, adds `src/commands/worklist.ts` +
   `worklist` in `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES`) and `e1cedba5` (20:12:33) landed
   afterwards. `grep -c worklist dist/cli.js` → `0`; `dist/commands/worklist.js`
   did not exist.

**Verification performed (reproduce → rebuild → pass):**

```bash
node dist/cli.js completion bash | grep -c worklist   # 0  (stale build)
npm run build
node dist/cli.js completion bash | grep -c worklist   # 2  (command + id-arg list)
node dist/cli.js completion zsh  | grep -c worklist   # 1
```

`worklist` is the **only** required command missing from the stale script
(`init status create list show update delete export import next in-progress
sync github comment close recent plugins migrate dep re-sort doctor search
unlock audit completion` all appear), which is exactly why the single
assertion that tripped names `worklist`.

**Why this is not simply "rebuild and move on":** a rebuild fixes this
checkout but commits nothing (`dist/` is gitignored), so the same false
failure returns for any checkout whose build lags `src/`. The repo already
solved this class of problem twice:

- WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 converted every `dist/cli.js`-spawning test to the
  pre-compiled bundle helper `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts` ("as a side effect now
  run against current `src/` instead of whatever build happened to be on
  disk") and added the regression guard `tests/unit/no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`
  — see `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`
  § "Change (test code + test config only)". **`completion.test.ts` was missed
  by that sweep.**
- WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U (same failure class, `entry-point-split.test.ts`) fixed
  `isDistFresh()` so `resolveStartupTarget('auto', …)` never selects a stale
  build.

So the durable fix is to finish the missed sweep for this file and make the
regression guard cover the *hard-coded `dist/` spawn* idiom, not only the
`tsx` idiom.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. From a checkout whose `dist/cli.js` predates the `worklist` command
   (`stat -c '%y' dist/cli.js` older than `git log -1 -- src/commands/worklist.ts`):
   - `npx vitest run tests/cli/completion.test.ts -t 'contains all known subcommands'`
2. Observe `expected completion script to contain "worklist"` for both the
   bash and zsh cases.
3. `npm run build` and re-run — both pass. (Confirmed during planning.)

## Desired Change

Keep it to test code, one new regression guard, and docs. No production code
change: `src/commands/completion.ts` already emits `worklist` correctly once
built from `HEAD`.

1. **Fix `tests/cli/completion.test.ts`** — resolve its CLI under test through
   the established, always-in-sync helper instead of `dist/cli.js`:
   `runCliProcess(['completion', 'bash'])` from `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts`
   (esbuild bundle of `src/cli.ts`, built once per test process, tsx fallback
   when esbuild is unavailable). Keep the existing assertions and the
   `--json`/unknown-shell/usage cases intact; only the spawn path changes.
2. **Extend the regression guard** — add `tests/unit/no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts`
   (modelled on `tests/unit/no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`): scan `tests/**/*.ts`
   for the `dist/cli.js` spawn idiom and fail for any file outside a
   documented allowlist, with a message pointing at
   `runCliProcess()`/`cliInvocation()`.
   - Allowlist rationale (each entry needs a one-line reason in the test):
     `tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts` and
     `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts` intentionally exercise the built
     entry (both go through the freshness-aware `resolveStartupTarget` /
     explicit-dist contract), `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts`
     uses temp fixtures, `tests/unit/no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts` is the scanner
     itself, and `tests/cli/smoke.test.ts` asserts that the *built* artefact
     loads — that is its purpose.
3. **Migrate the remaining hard-coded spawn** —
   `tests/cli/doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts` (`cliPath =
   path.join(projectRoot, 'dist', 'cli.js')`) should use `cliInvocation()`.
   If it proves load-bearing in a surprising way, allowlist it with a reason
   rather than blocking the guard.
4. **Docs** — update `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (§ the cli-bundle sweep)
   to record that `completion.test.ts` (+ `doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts`)
   now use the bundle, that `no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts` is the second guard,
   and to restate the standing rule: **tests must not hard-code `dist/cli.js`;
   `npm run build` is required before a bare checkout's suite, and the guard
   keeps that from silently producing false failures.**

## Implementation Notes (for implement phase)

- **Red-first evidence cannot come from the ambient checkout.** `implement.py`
  runs `npm run build` before tests, so in a worktree both shells already pass.
  Drive the guard test red by fixture: create a temp `tests/`-like tree (or
  pass a root parameter) containing a file that spawns `dist/cli.js` and assert
  the scanner reports it — mirror `startup-target-freshness.test.ts` (temp dirs
  + controlled content) rather than mutating real mtimes.
- **Alternative considered and rejected:** switch to
  `resolveStartupTarget('auto', repoRoot)` + `buildStartupInvocation(...)`.
  Correct, but slower than the bundle and leaves this file on the tsx fallback
  path when `dist/` is stale; the bundle is the repo's stated convention for
  "a real subprocess is needed".
- Completion output includes plugin-provided commands (e.g. `stats`) — plugin
  loading is independent of the entry point, so the bundle produces the same
  command list as `dist/cli.js`.
- Do **not** touch `src/commands/completion.ts`, `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` or
  `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts` — all three are already correct.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npx vitest run tests/cli/completion.test.ts` passes against the latest
  `dev` **both with a fresh `dist/` and with a deliberately stale/absent
  `dist/`** (the file no longer depends on ambient build state).
- [ ] `tests/cli/completion.test.ts` no longer hard-codes `dist/cli.js`; it
  spawns the CLI through `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts`
  (`runCliProcess`) and keeps every existing assertion (bash script shape,
  known subcommands, global options, dynamic work-item ID completion,
  completion-of-completion, unknown-shell error, `--json` payload) intact.
- [ ] A new guard test `tests/unit/no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts` fails when any
  test file outside a documented allowlist spawns a hard-coded `dist/cli.js`,
  and its failure message names the offending file and the recommended helper
  (red-first: proven against a fixture input, not only against the current
  tree).
- [ ] `tests/cli/doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts` either uses
  `cliInvocation()` or is allowlisted with a written reason.
- [ ] The two originally failing cases (`wl completion bash|zsh > contains all
  known subcommands`) pass, with `worklist` present in both generated scripts.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes
  (`docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`: cli-bundle sweep completeness, the new
  stale-dist guard, and the standing "tests must not hard-code `dist/`" rule).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Key Files

- `tests/cli/completion.test.ts` — spawn the CLI via `runCliProcess()`; drop `CLI_PATH`.
- `tests/unit/no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts` — new repo-wide guard (modelled on `no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`).
- `tests/cli/doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts` — remaining hard-coded `dist/cli.js` spawn; migrate or allowlist.
- `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts` — reused (`runCliProcess`/`cliInvocation`); no change expected.
- `tests/unit/no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts` — the guard pattern to mirror (read-only reference).
- `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts` — fixture-with-temp-dirs pattern for the guard's red-first evidence (read-only reference).
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — documentation update (sweep completeness + guard + standing rule).
- `src/commands/completion.ts` — verified correct; **no change expected**.

## Related work

- `WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF` — added the `worklist` command and the
  `worklist` entry in `KNOWN_COMMANDS` (commit `c8d8197f`); its suite run had a
  fresh build, which is why the gate was green and this checkout's stale
  `dist/` was not.
- `WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8` — the cli-bundle sweep + `no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`
  guard that this item completes.
- `WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U` — same failure class (`entry-point-split.test.ts`,
  stale `dist/`), fixed via `isDistFresh()`; establishes the
  "stale build is not a source defect; make tests independent of ambient
  build state" ruling.
- `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` — post-push verification item whose full-suite run in
  the advancing `dev` checkout first surfaced these two failures.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Assumption** — `runCliProcess()` reproduces `dist/cli.js`'s completion
  output exactly (same entry file, same command graph; only pre-compiled).
  Verified by the converted tests' assertions, which are unchanged.
- **Risk — esbuild unavailable → tsx fallback** makes the completion suite
  slower (~12 spawns), never wrong (`cli-bundle.ts` fails soft by design).
- **Risk — guard false positives** on files that legitimately test the build
  (three known sites). Mitigated by the documented allowlist above; new
  offenders get the migration message rather than a silent pass.
- **Assumption** — a production code change is *not* required. If the
  implement phase finds `completion.ts` genuinely omitting a registered command
  from `HEAD`'s build, that is a **new** defect: file it as a separate work
  item (`discovered-from` this one) instead of widening this scope.

## Plan notes

- The template ACs are preserved in intent and sharpened: AC1 keeps "the test
  passes on latest `dev`" but additionally requires independence from ambient
  build state (otherwise a rebuild — which commits nothing, `dist/` being
  gitignored — would satisfy it and the item would have no deliverable).
  AC2 keeps the docs requirement and names the exact file. AC3 keeps "full
  suite passes".
- The recurrence guard is the deliverable that makes this a real work item;
  it follows two completed precedents (`WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8`,
  `WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U`) rather than inventing a new mechanism.
- No children were created: effort Extra Small / risk Low, the change is one
  test file + one guard test + one doc, and it is a single vertical slice.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The plan pre-check returned `decision: "skip"` (effort **Extra Small**, risk
**Low**), and the root cause was established from repository evidence, so no
interview questions were required. Evidence reviewed:

- `tests/cli/completion.test.ts` (hard-coded `CLI_PATH = dist/cli.js`,
  `KNOWN_COMMANDS` incl. `worklist`).
- `src/commands/completion.ts` (introspects `program.commands`),
  `src/command-registry.ts` (`worklist` in `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES` /
  `COMMAND_LOADERS`; `FULL_REGISTRATION_COMMANDS = {completion}`).
- Live reproduction: stale `dist/cli.js` (mtime 15:52:42) → no `worklist`;
  after `npm run build` → `worklist` present in bash and zsh scripts.
- `git log --stat c8d8197f` (adds `src/commands/worklist.ts` and the
  `completion.test.ts` `+1 line` KNOWN_COMMANDS change), commit times vs
  `dist/cli.js` mtime.
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` `isDistFresh` / `resolveStartupTarget` (the
  existing freshness guard this file bypasses).
- `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts`, `tests/unit/no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`,
  `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (the established convention + guard
  pattern), `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts` (fixture pattern).
- Prior items `WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8`, `WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U`,
  `WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF` (their comments record the same failure class).
- Duplicate check: `wl search "completion worklist"` / `wl search "stale dist"`
  / `wl search "test stale build"` — no open item covers this gap;
  `WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U` is completed and scoped to `entry-point-split.test.ts`.

**OPEN QUESTION (none blocking; recorded for the producer's awareness):** the
plan assumes the fix stays test-only. If the producer wants the *whole* suite
to stop depending on ambient build state (i.e. make `npm test` build `dist/`
first, or make CI rebuild before the run), that is a broader policy change and
should be a separate work item — it is deliberately **not** in this scope.
